author: Anurag Singh
headline: Data Engineer @Fidelity | Snowflake ❄️ Architect/Data Engineer Certified | 3x Snowflake Certified | 3x Azure Certified
text:
My Zscaler Data Engineer Interview: Questions I Faced

I recently interviewed for a Data Engineer position at Zscaler and didn't get the offer. Instead of keeping quiet about it, I want to share the questions I encountered to help others prepare for similar roles.

The Technical Questions

SQL and Data Modeling
1. Design a star schema for analyzing network security events across multiple customers
2. Write a query to identify top 10 users by data transfer volume in the last 30 days
3. Optimize a slow query joining five large tables
4. Design a slowly changing dimension table for user attributes

Big Data and Distributed Systems
5. Explain how Apache Spark differs from MapReduce
6. Describe partitioning strategies for 100TB of security logs
7. How would you handle data skew in distributed processing?
8. Implement exactly-once semantics in a data pipeline

ETL and Pipeline Design
9. Design an ETL pipeline to ingest streaming security logs from thousands of endpoints
10. Handle late-arriving data in batch processing
11. Implement data quality checks across multi-stage pipelines
12. Design a retry mechanism for failed data loads

Real-Time Processing
13. Design a real-time analytics system for monitoring network threats globally
14. Handle backpressure when processing can't keep up with ingestion
15. Achieve low-latency querying on streaming data

Cloud and Data Warehousing
16. Compare data lake versus data warehouse for security analytics
17. Design a data retention strategy for petabyte-scale logs
18. Optimize cloud storage costs while maintaining query performance
19. Implement data archiving for compliance

Python and System Design
20. Parse and validate nested JSON log files efficiently
21. Process a 50GB CSV file without memory issues
22. Design a platform processing 100TB of security logs daily
23. Ensure data consistency across geographically distributed sources

Security and Compliance
24. Handle personally identifiable information in security logs
25. Implement role-based access control for data

My Takeaway

I struggled most with real-time processing architecture and system design at scale. This experience showed me clear gaps in my knowledge around petabyte-scale data processing.

Failure is feedback. On to strengthening these skills for the next opportunity.

Have you faced similar technical interviews? What helped you prepare?

headline: Sr. Data Engineer at Accenture Strategy |Ex-Deloitte, PwC | 3x Azure, 2x Databricks Certified | Transforming Data into Insights for Impact
text:
When I walked into my EY Data Engineer interview…..

I thought they’d ask basic questions like 𝗣𝘆𝘀𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗸 𝗦𝘆𝗻𝘁𝗮𝘅 𝗼𝗿 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝗦𝗤𝗟 𝗷𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘀.

But instead, they asked:-
If 10 million rows of data arrive daily from multiple regions, how would you design a scalable, cost-efficient data pipeline in the cloud?”

That’s when I realized — They’re not testing what you memorize. They’re testing how you think like a Data Engineer.

💡 What EY Technology Solutions Really Looks For:
It’s not about listing tools. It’s about showing that you can:

✅ Design resilient, scalable systems 
✅ Make thoughtful, real-world decisions 
✅ Translate tech into business impact

If you can explain why you made a choice — not just how — you’re already ahead.

This experience taught me that top-tier interviews are about engineering mindset, not just technical recall.

author: Raina Samiksha
headline: Senior Data Engineer | @Fractal Analytics |PySpark |Python |SQL Server and PL/SQL| Databricks | Azure Data Factory | DataLake | Delta Live table | ETL/ELT Pipelines
text:
“When a Late-Arriving Record Broke My SCD Type 2 Pipeline at 2 AM 😩”

It was 2 AM.
Our Databricks job failed — again.
A single record had arrived late.
 Its effective_date was older than the last one in the table.
 And just like that… our SCD Type 2 timeline broke. 😩

Instead of showing the customer’s true journey (Delhi → Noida → Pune),
 the data showed Delhi → Pune → Noida.
 The past and future were swapped.

That night, we fixed it with one small but powerful change. 

.whenMatchedUpdate(
 condition="s.effective_date BETWEEN t.effective_date AND COALESCE(t.end_date, '9999-12-31')",
 set={
 "t.end_date": "s.effective_date",
 "t.is_current": "false"
 }
)

💡 This tiny piece of logic did 3 things:
 ✅ Detected when data arrived late
 ✅ Closed the overlapping record
 ✅ Inserted the new record exactly where it belonged in time

Final table looked like this 👇
 Delhi → Noida → Pune ✅
 Perfect timeline. Truth preserved.

That’s when I realized —
 SCD Type 2 isn’t about versioning data.
 It’s about preserving reality. 
Because in the world of data,
 truth and order matter more than speed.
 The worst kind of data lie. 😬

💬 Have you ever had your timeline fall apart because of late-arriving data?
 How did you handle it? 👇

 Would love to hear your chaos story too. 😅

author: Jaydeep Patel
headline: Consultant Data & AI @ Deloitte USI, Analyst @ HCLTech, Data Engineer
text:
🍽️ Zomato Business Analyst Interview Experience — 18 LPA

Cracking the Zomato Business Analyst interview requires a mix of SQL mastery, product sense, and data-driven business thinking. Here’s a complete breakdown of how the interview rounds went 👇

⸻

🧩 Round 1: SQL + Data Analysis

Questions included:
 • Find customers who ordered from the same restaurant more than 3 times in a month.
 • Identify restaurants with increasing monthly revenue for the last 3 months.
 • Write a query to find repeat customers whose average order value exceeds the city average.
 • Calculate cancellation rate per city and identify top 3 cities with the worst rates.
 • Find the restaurant with maximum new customers this quarter.

🧠 Bonus Challenge:
“If a restaurant’s orders suddenly dropped by 30%, how would you diagnose the issue using SQL and data analysis?”

⸻

📊 Round 2: Business Case Study

Prompt:
“Zomato Gold usage has fallen by 20% in the last quarter. How would you identify the reason and fix it?”

Key areas to focus on:
 • Metrics: Renewal rate, ARPU, discount usage, and churn rate
 • Strategies: A/B testing, customer segmentation, retention incentives
 • Outcome: Clear linkage between business metrics and actionable insights

⸻

📈 Round 3: Product & Metrics Round
 • Define Zomato’s North Star Metric.
 • What KPIs would you track for delivery partner efficiency?
 • How would you measure the success of a new loyalty program?
 • If average delivery time increases by 10%, what downstream metrics will get affected?

⸻

💬 Round 4: Behavioral + Communication
 • Describe a time when data contradicted your initial assumption.
 • How do you simplify complex analyses for non-technical stakeholders?
 • How do you deal with incomplete or inconsistent data during analysis?

⸻

⚙️ Round 5: Excel + Dashboarding
 • Build a dashboard for daily orders, cancellations, and GMV trends.
 • Show how delivery delays correlate with customer churn using Power BI or Tableau.
 • Detect anomalies in datasets using pivot tables and calculated fields.

⸻

💼 Outcome:
Final offer — 18 LPA 💰
Strong fundamentals in SQL, structured thinking, and clear business reasoning made the difference.

⸻

📚 Preparation Focus:
✅ SQL (Joins, CTEs, Window Functions)
✅ Business metrics & case frameworks
✅ Visualization tools (Tableau, Power BI)
✅ Communication & storytelling with data
